  - std::string in C++ instead of C-style strings (strongly preferred)
  - gsl::span and gsl::string_span from Guideline Support Library
  - SafeInt library for integer overflow checks before allocation
  - strlcpy/strlcat (BSD-origin safe string functions)
  - Microsoft Safe CRT functions (strcpy_s, strcat_s, sprintf_s)
Prevention strategies:
  - Replace strcpy with strncpy/strlcpy and always null-terminate
  - Replace strcat with strncat/strlcat
  - Replace sprintf with snprintf
  - Replace gets with fgets (gets is removed in C11)
  - Use std::string in C++ instead of C-style strings
  - Enable stack protection: -fstack-protector-strong
  - Enable address sanitizer in testing: -fsanitize=address
  - Compile with -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 for runtime buffer overflow detection
  - Use Valgrind/ASan/MSan in CI/CD for memory safety testing
  - Follow C++ Core Guidelines and use the Guideline Support Library

title: Use-After-Free Vulnerability
description: Detects use-after-free vulnerabilities where heap-allocated memory is accessed after being freed, leading to dangling pointer dereferences. Attackers can reclaim the freed memory region with controlled data, enabling arbitrary read/write primitives, vtable hijacking in C++ objects, and ultimately remote code execution. This class of bug is among the most exploited in modern real-world attacks against browsers, kernels, and network daemons.
impact:
Use-after-free is one of the most dangerous memory corruption classes.
Exploitation enables arbitrary code execution through vtable hijacking,
heap metadata corruption, and function pointer overwrite. Attackers can
use heap spraying or feng shui techniques to reclaim freed memory with
controlled content, gaining reliable exploitation primitives. UAF bugs
account for a large proportion of real-world browser, kernel, and server
exploits. They can bypass ASLR when combined with information leaks and
defeat CFI/CET when exploiting virtual dispatch.
remediation:
Framework-specific fixes:
  - Modern C++: use std::unique_ptr for exclusive ownership, std::shared_ptr for shared ownership
  - Legacy C: always set pointers to NULL immediately after free()
  - Qt: use QPointer for guarded QObject pointers that auto-null on deletion
  - Chromium: use base::raw_ptr<T> or raw_ref<T> with BackupRefPtr (MiraclePtr)
Secure libraries:
  - Smart pointers (std::unique_ptr, std::shared_ptr, std::weak_ptr)
  - Guideline Support Library gsl::owner<T*> for ownership annotation
  - Boost.SmartPtr for cross-platform smart pointer support
  - Rust FFI bindings for memory-critical components
Prevention strategies:
  - Adopt RAII principles: tie resource lifetime to object lifetime
  - Set freed pointers to nullptr immediately after free/delete
  - Use AddressSanitizer (-fsanitize=address) to detect UAF at runtime
  - Use MemorySanitizer and UBSan for additional temporal safety checks
  - Enable Clang's -fsanitize=memory and -fsanitize=undefined in CI
  - Use static analyzers: Clang Static Analyzer, Coverity, Infer (Facebook)
  - Deploy with hardware-assisted tagging (ARM MTE) where available
  - Consider memory-safe language rewrites for critical parsing/network code
  - Enforce C++ Core Guidelines lifetime profiles via compiler tooling

title: Integer Overflow in Memory Allocation
description: Detects integer overflow or wraparound vulnerabilities in size calculations used for memory allocation. When an arithmetic operation on user-controlled values overflows before being passed to malloc, calloc, new, or similar allocators, the resulting buffer is undersized. Subsequent writes into this buffer using the original (pre-overflow) size cause heap buffer overflows, enabling heap corruption, arbitrary code execution, and denial of service.
impact:
Integer overflow in allocation sizes is a high-severity vulnerability class
that directly leads to heap buffer overflows. The undersized buffer is
filled using the original (non-overflowed) size, corrupting adjacent heap
chunks. This enables:
  - Heap metadata corruption for arbitrary write primitives
  - Overwriting adjacent heap-allocated objects (vtable pointers, function pointers)
  - Reliable exploitation via heap grooming/feng shui techniques
  - Denial of service through heap corruption and crashes
This vulnerability class has been exploited extensively in image parsers,
media codecs, network protocol implementations, and file format handlers.
remediation:
Framework-specific fixes:
  - GCC/Clang: use __builtin_mul_overflow() and __builtin_add_overflow() for checked arithmetic
  - MSVC: use SafeInt<T> or IntSafe.h (UIntMult, SizeTMult) from the Windows SDK
  - Chromium: use base::CheckedNumeric<T> or base::StrictNumeric<T>
  - Rust FFI: perform size calculations in Rust with checked arithmetic before calling C allocators
Secure libraries:
  - SafeInt library (Microsoft) for overflow-safe integer arithmetic
  - Boost.SafeNumerics for compile-time and runtime overflow detection
  - Google Abseil safe integer utilities (absl::uint128)
  - GCC/Clang __builtin_*_overflow family of builtins
  - CERT INT32-C compliant arithmetic wrappers
Prevention strategies:
  - Always validate that size * count and size + offset cannot overflow before allocation
  - Use calloc(count, size) which internally checks for overflow (on conforming implementations)
  - Prefer size_t for all size computations and check against SIZE_MAX / element_size
  - Set maximum allocation limits based on application context
  - Use AddressSanitizer to detect heap overflows from undersized allocations
  - Enable UBSan (-fsanitize=undefined) to trap signed integer overflow
  - Enable -ftrapv for signed overflow trapping in debug/test builds
  - Use static analysis tools (Coverity, PVS-Studio) to detect unchecked arithmetic
  - Fuzz allocation paths with AFL/libFuzzer to discover overflow-triggered crashes

title: Unvalidated Array Index
description: Detects array or buffer access using user-controlled indices without proper bounds validation. When an attacker controls the index used to read from or write to an array, they can achieve out-of-bounds read (information disclosure, ASLR bypass) or out-of-bounds write (arbitrary memory corruption, code execution). This is a prevalent vulnerability class in C/C++ due to the absence of automatic bounds checking on raw arrays and pointer arithmetic.
impact:
Unvalidated array indices enable two critical attack classes:
  - Out-of-bounds read: leaking sensitive data from adjacent memory,
    including cryptographic keys, session tokens, ASLR base addresses,
    and stack canary values. This can be chained with other exploits.
  - Out-of-bounds write: corrupting adjacent heap/stack objects including
    function pointers, vtable pointers, return addresses, and security-
    critical flags. This directly enables arbitrary code execution.
The Heartbleed vulnerability (CVE-2014-0160) is a canonical example of
OOB read via missing bounds check. Array index bugs in kernel drivers
frequently lead to local privilege escalation.
remediation:
Framework-specific fixes:
  - Modern C++: use std::vector::at() or std::array::at() for bounds-checked access
  - C++ GSL: use gsl::at() for bounds-checked array/span access
  - C: always validate index >= 0 && index < array_size before access
  - Qt: use QVector::value() with default return for safe out-of-range access
Secure libraries:
  - C++ Standard Library containers with .at() method (throws std::out_of_range)
  - gsl::span and gsl::at from Guideline Support Library
  - Boost.MultiArray with bounds-checked access modes
  - SafeInt for safe index arithmetic
Prevention strategies:
  - Always validate both lower bound (>= 0) and upper bound (< size) for indices
  - Use unsigned types (size_t) for indices and sizes to eliminate negative index attacks
  - Prefer range-based for loops over manual indexing
  - Use std::span (C++20) to carry size information with pointers
  - Enable UBSan (-fsanitize=undefined) for runtime out-of-bounds detection
  - Use ASan (-fsanitize=address) for heap/stack buffer overflow detection
  - Apply compiler hardening: -fbounds-checking (GCC), -fsanitize=bounds (Clang)
  - Use static analysis (Coverity, PVS-Studio, Polyspace) to detect missing bounds checks
  - Fuzz array access paths with AFL/libFuzzer to discover edge cases

title: Path Traversal via File Operations
description: Detects path traversal vulnerabilities in C++ file operations where user-controlled input is passed to fopen, ifstream, ofstream, or other file I/O functions without proper path validation. Attackers can use directory traversal sequences (../ or ..\) to escape intended directories, reading sensitive files such as /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, configuration files, private keys, or writing to arbitrary filesystem locations to overwrite executables, cron jobs, or configuration files.
impact:
Path traversal in C++ applications enables:
  - Arbitrary file read: accessing /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, SSH private keys,
    application source code, database credentials, and API secrets
  - Arbitrary file write: overwriting application binaries, cron jobs,
    authorized_keys files, web shells, or configuration files
  - Information disclosure: leaking source code, build artifacts, and internal
    data structures that aid further exploitation
  - Denial of service: deleting or corrupting critical system or application files
C++ applications frequently run as system services with elevated filesystem
permissions, making path traversal especially impactful. Combined with
file write capabilities, this can achieve remote code execution.
remediation:
Framework-specific fixes:
  - POSIX: use realpath() to canonicalize paths and verify they start with the allowed base directory
  - C++17: use std::filesystem::canonical() or weakly_canonical() for path normalization
  - Boost: use boost::filesystem::canonical() for path resolution
  - Windows: use GetFullPathNameW() and verify the canonical path is within the allowed directory
  - chroot jails: confine the process filesystem view to the intended directory tree
Secure libraries:
  - std::filesystem (C++17) for path manipulation with canonical()
  - boost::filesystem for cross-platform path canonicalization
  - libseccomp for restricting filesystem syscalls via seccomp-bpf
  - AppArmor/SELinux profiles for mandatory access control on file paths
Prevention strategies:
  - Canonicalize all user-provided paths with realpath()/std::filesystem::canonical()
  - Verify canonical path starts with the intended base directory prefix
  - Reject paths containing ".." components, absolute path prefixes, or null bytes
  - Use an allowlist of permitted filenames or path patterns
  - Strip or reject non-ASCII characters and control characters in filenames
  - Use chroot, containers, or namespace isolation to limit filesystem access
  - Apply principle of least privilege: run file-serving processes as unprivileged users
  - Use O_NOFOLLOW and O_NOTRAVERSE flags to prevent symlink-based traversal
  - Log and monitor file access patterns for anomalous traversal attempts

title: Unsafe Deserialization and Type Confusion
description: Detects type confusion and unsafe deserialization vulnerabilities in C++ where untrusted data is used to determine object types, drive unsafe casts, or reconstruct objects without proper type validation. Attackers can craft serialized input to instantiate unexpected types, corrupt vtable pointers via reinterpret_cast or C-style casts on untrusted data, or inject objects whose destructors or virtual methods execute attacker-controlled code. Type confusion is a critical vulnerability class in polymorphic C++ codebases, browser engines, and any application deserializing complex object graphs from untrusted sources.
impact:
Type confusion and unsafe deserialization in C++ enables:
  - Vtable hijacking: attacker-controlled data at the vtable pointer offset
    causes virtual method calls to jump to arbitrary addresses
  - Arbitrary read/write: accessing fields at wrong offsets reads or writes
    unintended memory locations
  - Remote code execution: the most common exploitation outcome, particularly
    in browser engines, media parsers, and network protocol handlers
  - Object injection: instantiating attacker-chosen types whose constructors
    or destructors have dangerous side effects
  - Information disclosure: reading fields at wrong offsets leaks pointers,
    keys, and other sensitive data from adjacent object fields
Type confusion bugs have been central to numerous high-profile exploits
including browser JIT engine attacks, PDF parser exploits, and kernel
driver vulnerabilities. They frequently bypass CFI when the confused types
share compatible call signatures.
remediation:
Framework-specific fixes:
  - C++: use dynamic_cast<Derived*>(base) for safe runtime-checked downcasts (returns nullptr on failure)
  - C++17: use std::variant with std::visit for type-safe discriminated unions
  - C++17: use std::any with std::any_cast which throws std::bad_any_cast on type mismatch
  - Protobuf/FlatBuffers/Cap'n Proto: use schema-validated deserialization instead of raw casts
Secure libraries:
  - Protocol Buffers (protobuf) for schema-validated serialization
  - FlatBuffers for zero-copy schema-validated deserialization
  - Cap'n Proto for capability-based serialization with type safety
  - cereal library for type-safe C++ serialization with class registration
  - Boost.Serialization with registered types and version control
  - nlohmann::json for structured text-based serialization
Prevention strategies:
  - Never use reinterpret_cast on untrusted data buffers
  - Always use dynamic_cast for polymorphic downcasts and check for nullptr
  - Validate type discriminators against an allowlist before casting
  - Use std::variant instead of unions for type-safe tagged unions
  - Implement schema validation before deserialization (validate before parse)
  - Use RTTI (typeid) or custom type registries for runtime type verification
  - Enable Clang CFI (-fsanitize=cfi) to detect type confusion at runtime
  - Use -fsanitize=undefined with -fsanitize=vptr for virtual call validation
  - Avoid placement new on untrusted buffers; copy data into constructed objects field by field
  - Use fuzzing with structure-aware mutators (libprotobuf-mutator) to test deserialization

title: C++ Buffer Overflow via strcpy
description: Detects use of unsafe string copy functions that can cause buffer overflow
impact: Buffer overflow can lead to arbitrary code execution and system compromise
remediation: Use strncpy, snprintf, or C++ std::string and std::string_view

title: C++ Format String Vulnerability
description: Detects format string vulnerabilities where user input controls format specifiers
impact: Format string attacks can read/write arbitrary memory, enabling code execution
remediation: Always use static format strings: printf("%s", user_input)

title: C++ Integer Overflow
description: Detects potential integer overflow in size calculations or allocations
impact: Integer overflow in allocations leads to heap overflow and code execution
remediation: Use overflow-checked arithmetic (__builtin_mul_overflow) before allocations

title: C++ Use After Free
description: Detects potential use-after-free patterns in C++
impact: Use-after-free enables arbitrary code execution through corrupted heap
remediation: Use std::unique_ptr/std::shared_ptr, set pointers to nullptr after deletion

title: C++ Double Free
description: Detects potential double-free vulnerabilities
impact: Double free corrupts heap metadata, enabling code execution
remediation: Use smart pointers (unique_ptr), always nullify pointers after free

title: C++ Hardcoded Credentials
description: Detects hardcoded passwords and API keys in C++ code
impact: Credentials in source can be extracted from compiled binaries
remediation: Use environment variables or OS-provided credential stores

title: C++ Weak Cryptography
description: Detects use of weak or deprecated crypto in C++
impact: Weak algorithms can be broken, compromising data confidentiality/integrity
remediation: Use EVP_aes_256_gcm for encryption, EVP_sha256+ for hashing

title: C++ Insecure Random Number Generation
description: Detects use of insecure PRNG for security-sensitive operations
impact: Predictable random numbers enable session prediction and key guessing
remediation: Use RAND_bytes (OpenSSL), std::random_device, or OS CSPRNG functions

title: C++ Path Traversal
description: Detects path traversal in C++ file operations
impact: Path traversal allows reading/writing arbitrary files
remediation: Use std::filesystem::canonical() and verify path is within allowed directory

title: C++ Unsafe Deserialization
description: Detects unsafe deserialization of untrusted data in C++
impact: Deserializing untrusted data can lead to memory corruption or code execution
remediation: Validate and limit deserialized data size, use schema validation

title: SQL Injection via String Concatenation in SqlCommand
description: Detects ADO.NET SqlCommand or Entity Framework raw SQL construction with concatenated user-controlled input. Covers SqlCommand, OleDbCommand, OdbcCommand, and EF Core raw SQL APIs where string interpolation or concatenation introduces tainted data into query strings without parameterization.
impact:
Full database compromise via SQL injection in .NET application.
May lead to data exfiltration, authentication bypass, data tampering,
and in severe cases, remote code execution via database features
such as xp_cmdshell on SQL Server.

title: Command Injection via Process.Start
description: Detects System.Diagnostics.Process.Start with user-controlled arguments enabling command injection. Covers direct Process.Start calls, ProcessStartInfo configuration, and shell invocation patterns where tainted input flows into process arguments or filenames without validation or sanitization.
impact:
Remote code execution via command injection in .NET application.
Complete server compromise, data exfiltration, lateral movement,
ransomware deployment, or persistent backdoor installation.

title: LDAP Injection via DirectorySearcher
description: Detects LDAP filter construction with concatenated user input in System.DirectoryServices queries. Covers DirectorySearcher, DirectoryEntry, PrincipalSearcher, and raw LDAP filter string building patterns where unsanitized input is embedded into LDAP query filters.
impact:
LDAP injection in Active Directory queries enabling authentication bypass
and unauthorized directory data access. May allow enumeration of all
directory users, extraction of sensitive attributes, and in some
configurations, modification of directory entries.

title: Unsafe Deserialization via BinaryFormatter
description: Detects use of BinaryFormatter, SoapFormatter, NetDataContractSerializer, ObjectStateFormatter, LosFormatter, or other unsafe deserialization APIs. These formatters allow arbitrary type instantiation during deserialization, enabling remote code execution through .NET gadget chains when processing untrusted data. BinaryFormatter has been officially deprecated in .NET 8+.
impact:
BinaryFormatter deserialization of untrusted data enables remote code
execution through .NET gadget chains (ysoserial.net). This is considered
one of the most severe vulnerability classes in .NET applications.
Full server compromise is typically achievable with known gadget chains.

title: XSS via Unencoded Response Output
description: Detects direct writing of user input to HTTP response without encoding in ASP.NET applications. Covers Response.Write, Html.Raw, Content() results, and ViewData/ViewBag rendering patterns where user-controlled data is reflected or stored without proper HTML encoding, enabling cross-site scripting attacks.
impact:
Cross-site scripting enabling session hijacking, credential theft,
and malicious code execution in user browsers. Stored XSS variants
affect all users who view the compromised content. May lead to
account takeover, data exfiltration, and phishing attacks.

title: MongoDB NoSQL Injection via Unsanitized Input (Python)
description: Detects MongoDB queries constructed with unsanitized user input in Python, including PyMongo find/aggregate with operator injection ($gt, $ne, $regex) and raw query string construction.
remediation: Use input validation and type coercion before passing to MongoDB queries. Never pass raw request.json as a MongoDB filter. Use schema validation (pydantic, marshmallow) to whitelist allowed fields. Convert expected ObjectId fields: bson.ObjectId(user_input). Reject any input containing MongoDB operators ($gt, $ne, etc.).

title: MongoDB NoSQL Injection (JavaScript/Node.js)
description: Detects MongoDB/Mongoose queries with unsanitized user input in Node.js applications. Attackers can inject MongoDB operators through JSON body parameters to bypass authentication or exfiltrate data.
remediation: Install express-mongo-sanitize middleware to strip MongoDB operators. Use Joi/Zod/Yup schema validation on all request inputs. Type-check inputs: use parseInt(), ObjectId(), etc. before queries. Never pass raw req.body as a MongoDB query filter.

title: MongoDB NoSQL Injection (Java)
description: Detects MongoDB queries in Java applications using Spring Data MongoDB or the native MongoDB Java driver with unsanitized user input.
remediation: Use Spring Data MongoDB repositories with derived query methods. Apply @Valid/@Validated annotations on request DTOs. Use MongoTemplate with type-safe Criteria builders.

title: LDAP Injection via Unsanitized Search Filter (Java)
description: Detects LDAP search filters constructed with string concatenation in Java. Attackers can inject LDAP filter metacharacters (* ( ) \\ / NUL) to modify query logic, bypass authentication, or enumerate directory entries.
remediation: Use OWASP ESAPI LdapEncoder.filterEncode() for filter values. Use Spring Security's LdapQueryBuilder for parameterized filters. Never concatenate user input into LDAP filter strings.

title: LDAP Injection (Python)
description: Detects LDAP filter construction with unsanitized user input in Python using python-ldap or ldap3 libraries.
remediation: Use ldap.filter.escape_filter_chars() to escape user input. For ldap3, use ldap3.utils.dn.escape_rdn() for DN components. Validate input against expected patterns (alphanumeric only).

title: XPath Injection (Java)
description: Detects XPath query construction with unsanitized user input in Java. XPath injection enables data extraction from XML documents including bypassing authentication in XML-based user stores.
remediation: Use XPathVariableResolver for parameterized XPath queries. Never concatenate user input into XPath expressions. Validate XML input against a schema before processing.

title: XPath Injection (Python)
remediation: Use lxml XPath variables: tree.xpath('//user[@name=$n]', n=user_input). Never use f-strings or .format() in XPath expressions.

title: GraphQL Query Injection (JavaScript)
description: Detects GraphQL queries constructed from unsanitized user input. Allows attackers to modify query structure, access unauthorized fields, perform introspection, or cause resource exhaustion via deeply nested queries.
remediation: Use GraphQL variables for all user input — never interpolate into query strings. Implement query depth limiting with graphql-depth-limit. Use query complexity analysis to prevent resource exhaustion. Disable introspection in production. Consider persisted/allowlisted queries.

title: GraphQL Query Injection (Python)
remediation: Use graphql-core's built-in validation. Pass user input as variables, not interpolated into query strings. Set max_depth and cost limits.

title: Server-Side Template Injection — Jinja2/Mako (Python)
description: Detects server-side template injection (SSTI) in Python applications using Jinja2 or Mako. SSTI enables arbitrary code execution on the server by injecting template directives ({{ }}, <% %>) into user-controlled template content.
remediation: Never pass user input as template content. Use render_template() with file-based templates and pass user data as context variables only. If dynamic templates are required, use jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment. Enable autoescape: Environment(autoescape=select_autoescape()).

title: Server-Side Template Injection — Freemarker/Thymeleaf/Pebble (Java)
remediation: Use file-based template resolution, never user-provided template names/content. For Thymeleaf, use th:text (escaped) instead of th:utext (unescaped). Disable dangerous built-ins in Freemarker: cfg.setNewBuiltinClassResolver(SAFER_RESOLVER).

title: Server-Side Template Injection (JavaScript/Node.js)
remediation: Never pass user input as template content. Use res.render() with file-based templates. Pass user data as template context variables only.

title: CRLF Injection / HTTP Response Splitting (Python)
description: Detects CRLF injection in Python web applications where user input flows into HTTP headers without sanitization. Enables HTTP response splitting, session fixation, and XSS via header injection.
remediation: Strip CR/LF characters from user input before header injection: value = user_input.replace('\r', '').replace('\n', ''). Use urllib.parse.quote() for URL-encoded header values. Modern frameworks (Django 3+, Flask 2+) auto-reject CRLF in headers.

title: CRLF Injection / HTTP Response Splitting (Java)
remediation: Use URLEncoder.encode() for URL parameters in redirects. Strip CR/LF: value.replaceAll("[\\r\\n]", ""). Use Spring's UriComponentsBuilder for safe URL construction.

title: Exploit Chain: Auth Bypass + SQL Injection → Database Takeover
description: Detects patterns where authentication bypass combined with SQL injection can lead to full database compromise
impact: Authentication bypass chained with SQL injection enables complete database takeover including data exfiltration, modification, and privilege escalation
remediation: Implement defense-in-depth: separate auth validation from data access, use parameterized queries even in authenticated contexts

title: Exploit Chain: Path Traversal + File Write → Remote Code Execution
description: Detects patterns where path traversal combined with file write can achieve code execution
impact: Attacker traverses to web-accessible directory and writes a web shell for full server compromise
remediation: Validate file paths strictly, restrict write directories, validate file extensions server-side, use randomized filenames

title: Exploit Chain: JWT Bypass + Admin Route → Privilege Escalation
description: Detects patterns where JWT validation weakness combined with admin-only routes enables privilege escalation
impact: JWT bypass allows forging admin tokens to access privileged endpoints and escalate to full system control
remediation: Enforce strong JWT verification with algorithm whitelist, validate claims server-side, implement RBAC checks beyond JWT

title: Exploit Chain: SSRF + Cloud Metadata → Credential Theft
description: Detects SSRF patterns that could reach cloud metadata endpoints for credential extraction
impact: SSRF to cloud metadata (AWS/GCP/Azure) exposes IAM credentials enabling cloud account takeover
remediation: Block requests to 169.254.169.254, use IMDSv2 (AWS), implement URL allowlisting

title: Exploit Chain: Deserialization + Gadget Chain → Remote Code Execution
description: Detects deserialization of untrusted data with available gadget chain libraries
impact: Deserialization with gadget chains enables arbitrary code execution through crafted serialized objects
remediation: Implement ObjectInputFilter, use JSON/protobuf instead, remove unnecessary gadget libraries from classpath

title: Exploit Chain: Stored XSS + Missing CSRF → Account Takeover
description: Detects stored XSS patterns that could be chained with CSRF to compromise user accounts
impact: Stored XSS combined with missing CSRF protection enables persistent session hijacking and account takeover at scale
remediation: Sanitize all stored user content with DOMPurify, implement CSRF tokens on all state-changing operations

title: Exploit Chain: IDOR + Sequential IDs → Mass Data Exfiltration
description: Detects IDOR patterns with sequential/enumerable identifiers that enable mass data scraping
impact: Sequential IDs without authorization checks allow automated enumeration of all records
remediation: Use UUIDs instead of sequential IDs, implement authorization checks on every data access

title: Exploit Chain: Log Injection + Log4Shell Pattern
description: Detects unsanitized user input in log statements that could enable log injection or Log4Shell-type attacks
impact: Log injection can forge log entries, and with Log4j JNDI lookups, enables RCE
remediation: Sanitize log input (remove newlines, JNDI patterns), use parameterized log4j format strings

title: SQL Injection via String Concatenation
description: Detects SQL query construction using fmt.Sprintf or string concatenation with user-controlled input instead of parameterized queries. This includes detection across database/sql, GORM, sqlx, ent, and other Go ORM/query builder libraries.
impact:
SQL injection enabling unauthorized data access, modification, deletion,
and potential command execution through database-specific features. May
lead to complete database compromise, data exfiltration, and lateral
movement within the infrastructure.

title: Command Injection via os/exec with User Input
description: Detects os/exec.Command with user-controlled input passed to shell interpreters or directly as command arguments. Covers exec.Command, exec.CommandContext, syscall.Exec, and os.StartProcess patterns across common Go web frameworks (net/http, gin, echo, chi, fiber).
impact:
Remote code execution on the server. An attacker can inject shell
metacharacters to execute arbitrary OS commands, potentially leading
to complete system compromise, data exfiltration, ransomware deployment,
or lateral movement within the network.

title: Template Injection via html/template or text/template
description: Detects Go template parsing with user-controlled template strings using text/template (which lacks auto-escaping) or html/template with user-controlled template definitions. Covers direct Parse calls, template composition abuse, and custom function map injection.
impact:
Server-side template injection in Go's text/template package allows
arbitrary function calls and data access through template actions.
Using text/template instead of html/template also enables XSS.
In severe cases, template injection can lead to information disclosure
of internal application state, secrets, and configuration.

title: LDAP Injection via Unsanitized Filter
description: Detects LDAP search filter construction with user-controlled input without proper escaping. Covers go-ldap, ldap.v3, and custom LDAP filter string construction patterns.
impact:
LDAP injection enables authentication bypass, unauthorized data access,
and information disclosure from directory services. Attackers can
enumerate users, extract email addresses and organizational data,
bypass access controls based on group membership, and in some cases
modify directory entries.

title: Unsafe Reflect or Plugin Loading
description: Detects dynamic code loading via plugin.Open or unsafe reflect operations with user-controlled input. Covers plugin loading, reflect-based method dispatch, dynamic type assertion, and unsafe pointer manipulation patterns that can lead to arbitrary code execution.
impact:
Dynamic plugin loading or reflection with user-controlled names can
execute arbitrary code or access unintended struct fields and methods.
Plugin injection leads to full remote code execution. Reflect-based
dispatch can bypass authorization by invoking admin-only methods,
and unsafe pointer manipulation can cause memory corruption or
information disclosure.

title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
description: Detects XML parsing in Go using encoding/xml or third-party XML libraries where external entity processing may lead to file disclosure or SSRF. Go's encoding/xml does not support external entities by default but third-party parsers (libxml2 bindings, etree) may be vulnerable.
impact:
XXE enables reading local files, SSRF to internal services, and DoS
via entity expansion. Go's stdlib is safe by default but third-party
XML libraries may be vulnerable.
remediation:
Use Go's encoding/xml which is safe by default. For third-party XML
libraries, disable external entity resolution. Prefer JSON over XML.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
description: Detects SSRF where user-controlled URLs are passed to http.Get, http.Post, http.Client.Do, or similar HTTP client functions enabling access to internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.
impact:
SSRF enables access to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints
(169.254.169.254), port scanning, and credential theft.
remediation:
Validate URLs against an allowlist. Block private IP ranges.
Use net.ParseIP to validate IP addresses. Implement DNS resolution
checks to prevent rebinding attacks.

title: Path Traversal in File Operations
description: Detects path traversal where user-controlled file paths are passed to os.Open, os.Create, ioutil.ReadFile, or http.ServeFile without proper sanitization via filepath.Clean or filepath.Base.
impact:
Path traversal enables reading arbitrary files (/etc/passwd, app config,
credentials), writing/overwriting files, and potentially RCE via
cron jobs or service configuration files.
remediation:
Use filepath.Base() to extract filename only. Use filepath.Clean() and
verify the result starts with the expected base directory. Use filepath.Join()
with a base directory and validate the resolved path stays within bounds.

title: Log Injection via Unsanitized User Input
description: Detects log injection where user-controlled input is written to log output without sanitization, enabling log forging, SIEM evasion, and potential log-based injection attacks.
impact:
Log injection enables log forging (fake log entries), SIEM evasion,
audit trail manipulation, and potential log-based injection if logs
are processed by other systems.
remediation:
Sanitize log input by replacing newlines and control characters.
Use structured logging (zap, logrus) with typed fields. Never
log raw user input without sanitization.

title: Open Redirect via User-Controlled URL
description: Detects open redirect vulnerabilities where user-controlled URLs are passed to http.Redirect or framework redirect functions without validating the destination against an allowlist.
impact:
Open redirect enables phishing attacks using the target domain's
reputation, OAuth token theft via redirect_uri manipulation, and
SSRF when redirect follows are automatic.
remediation:
Validate redirect URLs against an allowlist of domains. Only allow
relative redirects (starting with /). Use url.Parse to validate
the host before redirecting.

title: MongoDB NoSQL Injection
description: Detects NoSQL injection where user-controlled input is passed directly to MongoDB queries via the official Go driver, enabling query operator injection and authentication bypass.
impact:
NoSQL injection enables authentication bypass, data exfiltration, and
server-side JavaScript execution via $where operator.
remediation:
Validate input types strictly. Never pass raw JSON body as MongoDB filter.
Use explicit bson.M construction with validated values.

title: HTTP Header / CRLF Injection
description: Detects CRLF injection via user-controlled values in HTTP response headers using w.Header().Set(), w.Header().Add(), or framework header methods.
impact:
CRLF injection enables HTTP response splitting, XSS, cache poisoning,
and session fixation via injected Set-Cookie headers.
remediation:
Strip \\r and \\n from header values. Use url.QueryEscape() for
URL-based headers. Go 1.7+ net/http rejects headers with newlines.

title: Unsafe YAML Deserialization
description: Detects YAML unmarshaling of user-controlled data that may enable object instantiation attacks in Go applications using gopkg.in/yaml.v2 or gopkg.in/yaml.v3 with custom unmarshalers.
impact:
YAML deserialization can cause DoS via anchor expansion. Custom
unmarshalers may enable object instantiation attacks.
remediation:
Prefer JSON over YAML for API input. Use yaml.v3 with KnownFields(true)
to reject unexpected fields. Validate and size-limit input before parsing.

title: GraphQL Injection via Query Construction
description: Detects GraphQL query construction with user-controlled input via string concatenation or Sprintf, enabling query manipulation, introspection abuse, and resource exhaustion.
impact:
GraphQL injection enables unauthorized data access, introspection-based
schema enumeration, and DoS via deeply nested or aliased queries.
remediation:
Use parameterized GraphQL variables. Implement query complexity limits
and max depth. Disable introspection in production. Use persisted queries.

title: ReDoS via User-Controlled Regex Pattern
description: Detects regex compilation or matching with user-controlled patterns that may cause catastrophic backtracking. Go's regexp uses RE2 which is safe from backtracking, but regexp/syntax and third-party PCRE bindings are vulnerable.
impact:
ReDoS causes CPU exhaustion making the service unresponsive. Go's stdlib
regexp (RE2) is immune to backtracking but PCRE bindings are vulnerable.
remediation:
Use Go's stdlib regexp (RE2-based, immune to backtracking). Escape user
input with regexp.QuoteMeta(). If PCRE is needed, use context.WithTimeout.

title: SQL Injection via GString
description: Detects SQL injection via Groovy GString interpolation.
impact: GString interpolation in SQL queries leads to SQL injection.
remediation:
Use Groovy's parameterized SQL:
  sql.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", [userId])
  sql.rows("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = :name", [name: userName])

title: Command Injection via Execute
description: Detects OS command injection in Groovy.
impact: Injection attacks can lead to data breach, unauthorized access, or system compromise
remediation: Use parameterized queries, input validation, and output encoding

title: Groovy Script Injection (eval/GroovyShell)
description: Detects dynamic Groovy code execution with user input.
impact: Groovy script injection enables arbitrary code execution on the server.

title: XXE in Groovy XML Parsing
description: Detects XML parsing without disabling external entities.
impact: Injection attacks can lead to data breach, unauthorized access, or system compromise
remediation: Use parameterized queries, input validation, and output encoding

title: Hardcoded Credentials in Groovy
description: Detects hardcoded passwords and secrets in Groovy code.
impact: Authentication and authorization flaws can lead to unauthorized access and privilege escalation
remediation: Implement strong authentication, proper session management, and principle of least privilege

title: Weak Cryptography in Groovy
description: Detects weak cryptographic algorithms.
impact: Weak cryptography can be broken, compromising data confidentiality and integrity
remediation: Use industry-standard algorithms (AES-256-GCM, SHA-256+, Argon2) and proper key management

title: Unsafe Deserialization in Groovy
description: Detects unsafe Java deserialization in Groovy.
impact: Unsafe deserialization can lead to remote code execution via gadget chains
remediation: Use safe serialization formats (JSON), implement type filtering, avoid deserializing untrusted data

title: Path Traversal in Groovy
description: Detects file access with user-controlled paths.
impact: Path traversal enables reading or writing arbitrary files on the server
remediation: Canonicalize paths and verify they remain within expected base directories

title: XSS in Grails/Groovy Templates
description: Detects XSS in Grails GSP templates.
impact: Cross-site scripting enables session hijacking, credential theft, and website defacement
remediation: Apply context-aware output encoding and use Content Security Policy headers

title: Server-Side Request Forgery
description: Detects HTTP requests with user-controlled URLs.
impact: Server-side request forgery enables access to internal resources and cloud metadata
remediation: Validate and allowlist URLs, block private IP ranges and cloud metadata endpoints

title: Jenkins Pipeline Credential Exposure
description: Detects credential exposure in Jenkins pipeline Groovy scripts.
impact: Exposed secrets enable unauthorized access to systems, APIs, and sensitive data
remediation: Use secret management systems, environment variables, and rotate exposed credentials immediately

title: Jenkins Insecure Script Approval
description: Detects Jenkins pipeline scripts using unsafe methods.
impact: Framework misconfiguration can disable security controls and expose sensitive functionality
remediation: Follow framework security best practices, enable security features, review configuration

title: SQL Injection via String Concatenation in Statement
description: Detects JDBC Statement.execute or createStatement with concatenated user input instead of PreparedStatement. This includes detection of string-built queries passed to Statement objects, StringBuilder-based query assembly, and indirect taint flows from HTTP request parameters into SQL execution sinks.
impact:
SQL injection via JDBC Statement allows full database compromise including
data exfiltration, record manipulation, schema modification, and in some
cases remote code execution through database stored procedures.

title: Command Injection via Runtime.exec or ProcessBuilder
description: Detects Runtime.exec() or ProcessBuilder.command() with user-controlled input enabling OS command injection. Covers direct invocations, shell wrappers (cmd.exe /c, /bin/sh -c), indirect taint through variable assignment, and commons-exec usage with unsanitized arguments.
impact:
Arbitrary OS command execution on the server, enabling full system compromise,
data exfiltration, privilege escalation, and lateral movement.

title: JNDI Injection (Log4Shell Pattern)
description: Detects potential JNDI lookup injection through user-controlled input passed to logging frameworks or JNDI context lookups. Covers Log4j2 message lookup exploitation (CVE-2021-44228), direct InitialContext.lookup with tainted strings, JMS destination lookups, and DataSource JNDI references with user-influenced names.
impact:
JNDI injection (CVE-2021-44228 — Log4Shell) enables remote code execution
by triggering JNDI lookups to attacker-controlled LDAP/RMI servers, which
serve malicious Java classes for deserialization.

title: Expression Language Injection (SpEL/EL)
description: Detects Spring Expression Language (SpEL) or Jakarta Expression Language (EL) evaluation with user-controlled input. Covers SpelExpressionParser, StandardEvaluationContext, @Value annotations with tainted input, Thymeleaf expression injection, and JSP EL injection via dynamic attribute construction.
impact:
SpEL injection allows arbitrary code execution within the Spring application
context, enabling access to runtime objects, bean manipulation, file system
access, and remote code execution.

title: HQL/JPQL Injection via String Concatenation
description: Detects Hibernate HQL or JPA JPQL query construction via string concatenation with user-controlled input. Covers EntityManager.createQuery, Session.createQuery, createNativeQuery, dynamic Criteria API misuse, and Spring Data JPA @Query with SpEL or concatenation-based construction.
impact:
HQL/JPQL injection can bypass ORM protections when queries are constructed
via concatenation. While more limited than raw SQL injection, it still
enables unauthorized data access and manipulation.

title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
description: Detects XML parsing with external entity processing enabled via DocumentBuilderFactory, SAXParserFactory, XMLInputFactory, or TransformerFactory without proper feature disabling.
impact:
XXE enables reading local files, SSRF to internal services, denial of
service via billion laughs, and port scanning of internal networks.

title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
description: Detects template rendering with user-controlled template strings in Freemarker, Velocity, Pebble, or Thymeleaf enabling arbitrary code execution.
impact:
SSTI in Java template engines allows arbitrary code execution via
reflection, class loading, and Runtime.exec() through template expressions.
remediation:
Never render user-controlled strings as templates. Use file-based template
resolution with ClassLoaderTemplateResolver or FileTemplateLoader. For
Freemarker, set new_builtin_class_resolver to TemplateClassResolver.SAFER_RESOLVER.

title: Unsafe Deserialization via ObjectInputStream
description: Detects Java deserialization of untrusted data via ObjectInputStream.readObject(), XMLDecoder, or third-party libraries (Kryo, Hessian, XStream) without deserialization filters.
impact:
Java deserialization leads to RCE via gadget chains (commons-collections,
Spring, Hibernate). Full server compromise is achievable.
remediation:
Use ObjectInputFilter (Java 9+) to restrict deserializable classes.
Use ValidatingObjectInputStream from Apache Commons IO. Prefer JSON
serialization (Jackson, Gson) over Java serialization. Remove unused
gadget chain libraries from classpath.

title: XPath Injection via String Concatenation
description: Detects XPath query construction with user-controlled input via string concatenation in javax.xml.xpath.XPath evaluate/compile calls.
impact:
XPath injection enables extraction of arbitrary XML data and
authentication bypass in XML-based data stores.

title: LDAP Injection via String Concatenation
description: Detects LDAP search filter or DN construction via string concatenation with user-controlled input in javax.naming or Spring LDAP APIs.
impact:
LDAP injection allows authentication bypass, user enumeration, and
extraction of directory attributes including passwords and group memberships.
remediation:
Use LdapEncoder.filterEncode() from Spring LDAP for filter values.
Use LdapNameBuilder for DN construction. Apply strict input validation.

title: HTTP Header / CRLF Injection
description: Detects HTTP response header injection via user-controlled values in setHeader, addHeader, sendRedirect, or addCookie enabling CRLF injection.
impact:
CRLF injection enables HTTP response splitting, XSS via injected headers,
cache poisoning, and session fixation attacks.
remediation:
Use URLEncoder.encode() or Spring's UriUtils.encode() for header values.
Strip \\r and \\n characters. Use framework redirect methods instead of
manual Location headers.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
description: Detects SSRF where user-controlled URLs are passed to URL, HttpClient, RestTemplate, or WebClient enabling access to internal services.
impact:
SSRF enables access to internal services (databases, admin panels, cloud
metadata), port scanning, and credential theft from metadata endpoints.
remediation:
Validate URLs against an allowlist of permitted domains. Block access to
private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x, localhost).
Use DNS resolution validation to prevent DNS rebinding.

title: ScriptEngine / Groovy Code Injection
description: Detects code injection through javax.script.ScriptEngine.eval(), GroovyShell.evaluate(), or BeanShell Interpreter.eval() with user input.
impact:
Script engine injection provides full JVM code execution including
Runtime.exec(), file I/O, network access, and reflection capabilities.
remediation:
Never evaluate user-controlled scripts. Use Groovy SecureASTCustomizer
with CompilerConfiguration for restricted execution. Prefer typed APIs
over scripting engines.

title: MyBatis ${} SQL Injection
description: Detects MyBatis mapper XML or annotation queries using ${} interpolation instead of #{} parameterization, enabling SQL injection.
impact:
MyBatis ${} performs raw string interpolation into SQL enabling full SQL
injection including UNION attacks, data exfiltration, and RCE via DB features.
remediation:
Always use #{} for parameterized values. For dynamic ORDER BY or table names,
use MyBatis <choose>/<when> with allowlisted values or a Java-side allowlist map.

title: Reflection-based Method Invocation Injection
description: Detects use of Java reflection (Class.forName, Method.invoke, Constructor.newInstance) with user-controlled class names, method names, or arguments enabling arbitrary code execution.
impact:
Reflection injection enables arbitrary class loading and method invocation,
leading to RCE via Runtime.exec(), file access, and system compromise.
remediation:
Use strict allowlists for permitted class and method names. Replace
reflection with typed dispatch maps or strategy pattern. Never use
Class.forName with user input directly.

title: innerHTML/outerHTML DOM XSS Injection
description: Detects assignment of user-controlled input to innerHTML or outerHTML properties, enabling DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting. These properties parse HTML strings and execute embedded scripts, allowing attackers to inject malicious markup that executes in the victim's browser context.
impact:
DOM XSS via innerHTML allows attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript
in the victim's browser, enabling session hijacking, credential theft,
keylogging, phishing overlays, and cryptocurrency mining.
remediation:
- Use textContent or innerText instead of innerHTML for text.
- Sanitize HTML with DOMPurify before innerHTML assignment.
- Use Content Security Policy headers to mitigate impact.
- Use frameworks with automatic escaping (React, Vue, Angular).

title: eval() with User-Controlled Input
description: Detects usage of JavaScript eval() function where the argument may contain user-controlled input. eval() interprets strings as JavaScript code, enabling arbitrary code execution when untrusted data is passed to it.
impact:
Arbitrary JavaScript code execution enabling RCE on Node.js servers,
data exfiltration, credential theft, and full system compromise. On
client-side, enables complete session takeover.
remediation:
- Never use eval() with user input. Use JSON.parse() for JSON.
- Use safe expression evaluators (mathjs, expr-eval).
- Implement Content Security Policy with script-src restrictions.
- Use vm2 or isolated-vm for sandboxed code execution.

title: Function Constructor Injection
description: Detects use of the Function constructor with user-controlled strings. new Function(code) is equivalent to eval() and executes arbitrary JavaScript. Attackers can inject code through function body arguments.
impact:
Function constructor injection enables arbitrary JavaScript execution,
identical to eval() in impact. On Node.js, this leads to full RCE.
remediation:
- Never pass user input to new Function().
- Use safe expression parsers (mathjs, expr-eval).
- Apply CSP headers to restrict inline script execution.

title: setTimeout/setInterval String Argument Injection
description: Detects setTimeout or setInterval called with a string argument containing user input. When passed a string, these functions evaluate it as code, equivalent to eval().
impact:
Arbitrary JavaScript execution via timer functions when string arguments
are used instead of function references. Enables XSS and session hijacking.
remediation:
- Always pass function references to setTimeout/setInterval, never strings.
- Use arrow functions: setTimeout(() => action(), delay).
- Enable ESLint no-implied-eval rule.

title: document.write DOM Injection
description: Detects document.write() or document.writeln() with user-controlled input. These functions directly inject HTML into the page, enabling DOM XSS when unsanitized user data is included.
impact:
document.write with user input enables DOM-based XSS, allowing attackers
to inject scripts, steal credentials, and hijack sessions.
remediation:
- Avoid document.write(); use DOM manipulation APIs instead.
- Sanitize content with DOMPurify before writing.
- Use textContent for text-only output.

title: Template Literal SQL Injection in Node.js
description: Detects SQL queries constructed using template literals or string concatenation with user-controlled input in Node.js applications. This enables SQL injection attacks against backend databases.
impact:
SQL injection allows attackers to read, modify, or delete database
records, bypass authentication, and potentially execute OS commands
via database-specific features.
remediation:
- Use parameterized queries: db.query('SELECT * WHERE id = ?', [id]).
- Use ORM query builders (Knex, Sequelize, TypeORM) instead of raw SQL.
- Validate and sanitize all user input used in queries.

title: child_process.exec Command Injection
description: Detects command injection via Node.js child_process.exec, execSync, or spawn with shell:true where user-controlled input is passed as part of the command string. exec() passes the command through a shell interpreter, enabling injection of shell metacharacters for arbitrary command execution.
impact:
Arbitrary OS command execution enabling full server compromise, data
exfiltration, lateral movement, ransomware deployment, and persistent
backdoor installation.
remediation:
- Use execFile() or spawn() without shell:true for safe execution.
- Pass arguments as arrays, never as concatenated strings.
- Validate input against strict allowlists.
- Use shell-escape or shell-quote library for unavoidable shell usage.

title: Prototype Pollution via Object Merge/Extend
description: Detects prototype pollution vulnerabilities where user-controlled objects are merged into application objects using recursive merge, deep extend, or Object.assign patterns. Attackers can inject __proto__, constructor, or prototype properties to modify Object.prototype, affecting all objects.
impact:
Prototype pollution can modify behavior of all JavaScript objects,
enabling RCE (via gadget chains), authentication bypass, XSS, and DoS.
remediation:
- Use Object.create(null) for dictionary objects.
- Freeze prototypes with Object.freeze(Object.prototype).
- Use Map instead of plain objects for user-controlled keys.
- Validate and strip __proto__, constructor, prototype keys from input.

title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
description: Detects SSTI vulnerabilities in Node.js template engines (EJS, Pug, Handlebars, Nunjucks) where user-controlled input is used as template content rather than template data, enabling arbitrary code execution.
impact:
SSTI in Node.js template engines enables arbitrary code execution on the
server, leading to full system compromise, data exfiltration, and RCE.
remediation:
- Never use user input as template content; only pass it as template data.
- Use res.render(viewName, {data}) with predefined template files.
- Enable sandboxed template execution where available.
- Use logic-less templates (Mustache) that don't support code execution.

title: MongoDB NoSQL Injection
description: Detects NoSQL injection in MongoDB queries where user-controlled input is passed directly to MongoDB operators like $where, $regex, $gt, $ne, enabling query manipulation, authentication bypass, and data exfiltration.
impact:
NoSQL injection allows attackers to bypass authentication, extract data,
modify queries, and potentially execute server-side JavaScript via $where.
remediation:
- Use express-mongo-sanitize middleware.
- Validate input types strictly (expect string, reject objects).
- Never pass raw request body/query to MongoDB operations.
- Use MongoDB parameterized queries and avoid $where.

title: RegExp Constructor ReDoS Injection
description: Detects usage of the RegExp constructor with user-controlled patterns, enabling Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) attacks. Attackers can craft patterns with exponential backtracking complexity.
impact:
ReDoS attacks cause CPU exhaustion, making the application unresponsive.
Attackers can craft patterns that take exponential time to evaluate.
remediation:
- Escape user input with escapeRegExp before using in RegExp constructor.
- Use re2 library for safe regex evaluation.
- Set timeouts on regex operations.
- Use safe-regex to validate patterns before execution.

title: postMessage Origin Bypass Injection
description: Detects insecure postMessage handling where the origin of incoming messages is not validated, allowing cross-origin attackers to inject malicious data or trigger unauthorized actions.
impact:
Missing postMessage origin validation allows cross-origin attackers to
inject data, trigger XSS, forge actions, and steal sensitive information.
remediation:
- Always validate event.origin against a strict allowlist.
- Never use '*' as the target origin in postMessage().
- Validate and sanitize event.data before processing.

title: WebSocket Message Injection
description: Detects insecure handling of WebSocket messages where incoming data is used without validation in security-sensitive operations like eval, innerHTML, or database queries.
impact:
WebSocket message injection can lead to code execution, XSS, SQL
injection, and unauthorized data manipulation in real-time applications.
remediation:
- Validate and sanitize all WebSocket message data.
- Use schema validation (Joi, ajv) for message formats.
- Never use eval() or innerHTML with WebSocket data.
- Implement message authentication (HMAC signatures).

title: Express Middleware Body Parser Injection
description: Detects insecure Express.js middleware configurations that allow body parser type confusion attacks, enabling attackers to send unexpected content types that bypass validation logic.
impact:
Insecure body parser configuration enables type confusion attacks,
prototype pollution via extended urlencoded, and content-type bypass.
remediation:
- Use extended: false for urlencoded parser.
- Set explicit content type restrictions.
- Validate req.body types explicitly in route handlers.
- Use express-mongo-sanitize to prevent operator injection.

title: LDAP Injection via ldapjs
description: Detects LDAP injection vulnerabilities in Node.js applications using ldapjs or similar LDAP client libraries where user-controlled input is interpolated into LDAP filter strings without sanitization.
impact:
LDAP injection allows attackers to bypass authentication, enumerate
directory users, extract sensitive attributes, and modify directory entries.
remediation:
- Use LDAP filter escaping functions for user input.
- Use ldapjs Filter objects instead of string filters.
- Validate input against strict character allowlists.
- Use parameterized LDAP queries where available.

title: Kotlin SQL Injection via String Template
description: Detects SQL queries built using Kotlin string templates with user input
impact: SQL injection can lead to data breach, data manipulation, or full database compromise
remediation: Use parameterized queries via Room DAO, Exposed framework, or PreparedStatement

title: Kotlin Command Injection
description: Detects OS command execution with user-controlled input in Kotlin
impact: Remote code execution on the server
remediation: Use ProcessBuilder with explicit argument list, validate and sanitize all inputs

title: Kotlin LDAP Injection
description: Detects LDAP queries built with user input in Kotlin
impact: LDAP injection can bypass authentication or leak directory information
remediation: Use LDAP SDK filter builders or escape special characters with LDAPFilter

title: Kotlin NoSQL Injection
description: Detects MongoDB/NoSQL queries with string interpolation
impact: NoSQL injection can lead to data exfiltration or authentication bypass
remediation: Use MongoDB Kotlin driver filter builders like Filters.eq(), Filters.and()

title: Kotlin XSS via Template Response
description: Detects reflected user input in Kotlin web responses without encoding
impact: Cross-site scripting can steal session tokens or deface the application
remediation: Use HTML encoding libraries or Ktor's templating engines with auto-escaping

title: Kotlin Exposed Framework Raw SQL
description: Detects raw SQL usage in Kotlin Exposed framework
impact: SQL injection via raw queries in Exposed framework bypasses the ORM's safety
remediation: Use Exposed's type-safe DSL (Table.select, Table.insert) instead of raw SQL

title: Kotlin Ktor Path Parameter Injection
description: Detects unsafe use of Ktor route parameters in database queries or command execution
impact: Route parameters used directly in queries enable injection attacks
remediation: Validate and type-convert path parameters, use parameterized queries

title: Kotlin Hardcoded Credentials
description: Detects hardcoded passwords, API keys, or tokens in Kotlin source code
impact: Hardcoded credentials in source code can be extracted from compiled applications
remediation: Use environment variables, Android Keystore, or secure vault systems

title: Kotlin Insecure JWT Validation
description: Detects JWT validation without proper signature verification in Kotlin
impact: Insecure JWT validation allows attackers to forge authentication tokens
remediation: Always verify JWT signatures with strong keys, validate claims (exp, iss, aud)

title: Kotlin Weak Cryptography
description: Detects use of weak or broken cryptographic algorithms in Kotlin
impact: Weak cryptographic algorithms can be broken, compromising data confidentiality
remediation: Use AES-256-GCM for encryption, SHA-256+ for hashing, and Argon2 for passwords

title: Kotlin Unsafe Deserialization
description: Detects unsafe deserialization of untrusted data in Kotlin
impact: Unsafe deserialization can lead to remote code execution
remediation: Use kotlinx.serialization with specific types, implement ObjectInputFilter

title: Kotlin Server-Side Request Forgery
description: Detects SSRF vulnerabilities in Kotlin HTTP client calls
impact: SSRF allows attackers to make requests to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints
remediation: Validate and whitelist allowed URLs/hosts, block internal IP ranges

title: Kotlin Path Traversal
description: Detects path traversal vulnerabilities in Kotlin file operations
impact: Path traversal allows reading or writing arbitrary files on the server
remediation: Canonicalize paths and verify they start with the expected base directory

title: SQL Injection via NSString Format
description: Detects SQL queries built using NSString formatting with user input.
impact: SQL injection via NSString formatting allows data theft and RCE.
remediation:
Use parameterized queries with FMDB:
  [db executeQuery:@"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?" withArgumentsInArray:@[@(userId)]];

title: Command Injection via NSTask
description: Detects OS command execution with user-controlled arguments.
impact: Command injection allows execution of arbitrary OS commands.
remediation: Use NSTask with explicit argument arrays. Never pass user input to system() or popen().

title: Format String Vulnerability
description: Detects format string vulnerabilities in Objective-C.
impact: Format string vulnerabilities can cause crashes, info leaks, and code execution.

title: Predicate Injection (NSPredicate)
description: Detects NSPredicate injection with user-controlled filter strings.
impact: Predicate injection can bypass data filters and access unauthorized CoreData records.
remediation:
Use parameterized predicates:
  [NSPredicate predicateWithFormat:@"name == %@", userInput];

title: Insecure Keychain Storage
description: Detects insecure Keychain access configuration.
impact: Insecure Keychain accessibility allows data theft from locked devices.
remediation:
Use the most restrictive accessibility:
  kSecAttrAccessibleWhenPasscodeSetThisDeviceOnly

title: Disabled App Transport Security
description: Detects disabled ATS allowing insecure HTTP connections.
impact: Disabled ATS allows unencrypted HTTP traffic, enabling MITM attacks.
remediation: Enable ATS and only add exceptions for specific domains that require HTTP.

title: Hardcoded Credentials
description: Detects hardcoded passwords, API keys, or secrets in Objective-C code.
impact: Authentication and authorization flaws can lead to unauthorized access and privilege escalation
remediation: Implement strong authentication, proper session management, and principle of least privilege

title: Weak Cryptographic Algorithm
description: Detects use of weak cryptographic algorithms in Objective-C.
impact: Weak cryptographic algorithms are vulnerable to brute force and collision attacks.

title: Insecure Random Number Generator
description: Detects use of rand(), random(), or arc4random() for security-sensitive purposes.
impact: Predictable random values compromise tokens, keys, and nonces.
remediation:
Use SecRandomCopyBytes for cryptographic randomness:
  SecRandomCopyBytes(kSecRandomDefault, count, bytes);

title: Insecure TLS Configuration
description: Detects disabled SSL/TLS certificate validation.
impact: Weak cryptography can be broken, compromising data confidentiality and integrity
remediation: Use industry-standard algorithms (AES-256-GCM, SHA-256+, Argon2) and proper key management

title: Path Traversal via User Input
description: Detects file operations with user-controlled paths.
impact: Path traversal enables reading or writing arbitrary files on the server
remediation: Canonicalize paths and verify they remain within expected base directories

title: Unsafe NSKeyedUnarchiver
description: Detects unsafe unarchiving of untrusted data without class validation.
impact: Unsafe deserialization can lead to arbitrary code execution.

title: XSS via UIWebView/WKWebView
description: Detects XSS via loading untrusted HTML in web views.
impact: Cross-site scripting enables session hijacking, credential theft, and website defacement
remediation: Apply context-aware output encoding and use Content Security Policy headers

title: Sensitive Data in NSUserDefaults
description: Detects storage of sensitive data in unencrypted NSUserDefaults.
impact: NSUserDefaults stores data unencrypted and can be accessed by iTunes backups.
remediation:
Store sensitive data in the Keychain instead:
  SecItemAdd(query, nil)

title: Deprecated UIWebView Usage
description: Detects use of deprecated UIWebView which has security issues.
impact: UIWebView is deprecated and has known security vulnerabilities.
remediation: Migrate to WKWebView which has better security features.

title: JavaScript Bridge Without Validation
description: Detects WKWebView JavaScript bridge without message validation.
impact: Framework misconfiguration can disable security controls and expose sensitive functionality
remediation: Follow framework security best practices, enable security features, review configuration

title: SQL Injection via String Interpolation
description: Detects SQL queries built with PHP string interpolation or concatenation with user-controlled input ($_GET, $_POST, $_REQUEST). Identifies both direct superglobal usage and indirect tainted variable flow into query construction across legacy mysql_, mysqli, PDO raw query, and pg_ APIs.
impact:
Complete database compromise including data theft, unauthorized modification,
authentication bypass, and potential RCE via INTO OUTFILE or LOAD_FILE.

title: Command Injection via system/exec/passthru
description: Detects PHP command execution functions (system, exec, passthru, shell_exec, popen, proc_open, backtick operator) receiving user-controlled input directly or through string concatenation. Also detects indirect command injection through variables derived from superglobals without proper escaping via escapeshellarg/escapeshellcmd.
impact:
Arbitrary OS command execution enabling full server compromise,
data exfiltration, lateral movement, and persistent backdoor installation.

title: Code Injection via eval/assert/preg_replace-e
description: Detects PHP code injection through eval(), assert(), create_function(), preg_replace with /e modifier, or dynamic function invocation patterns such as $func() and call_user_func() where the function name or code body is derived from user-controlled input. Includes detection of obfuscated eval patterns using base64_decode, gzinflate, and similar encoding/compression wrappers commonly seen in webshells.
impact:
Arbitrary PHP code execution in the application context with full
access to the file system, database, and network. Can lead to
webshell installation, data exfiltration, and full server compromise.

title: File Inclusion via include/require with User Input
description: Detects local file inclusion (LFI) and remote file inclusion (RFI) vulnerabilities through include, include_once, require, or require_once statements that incorporate user-controlled input in the file path. Covers direct superglobal usage, tainted variable intermediaries, and path traversal patterns (../) in included paths. Also detects indirect inclusion through variable variables and dynamic path construction.
impact:
Local File Inclusion (LFI) allows reading arbitrary server files
(/etc/passwd, PHP source code, configuration files with credentials).
Remote File Inclusion (RFI) enables executing attacker-hosted PHP code
on the server, resulting in full compromise. PHP wrapper attacks
(php://filter) can disclose source code even with restrictive configs.

title: XPath Injection via Unsanitized Input
description: Detects XPath query construction with user-controlled input through string concatenation or interpolation. XPath injection targets applications that use XML data stores or process XML documents using DOMXPath or SimpleXML xpath methods. Covers direct superglobal injection, tainted variable flow, and dynamically constructed XPath predicates used in authentication, authorization, or data retrieval contexts.
impact:
XPath injection allows authentication bypass, unauthorized data extraction,
and information disclosure from XML data stores. Complete XML document
enumeration is possible through boolean-based blind XPath injection.
Unlike SQL injection, XPath has no access control so the entire
document is always accessible once injection is achieved.

title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
description: Detects XXE vulnerabilities where XML parsers (simplexml_load_string, DOMDocument::loadXML, xml_parse) process user-controlled XML without disabling external entity loading. PHP's libxml is vulnerable by default in versions prior to PHP 8.0. Covers simplexml, DOM, XMLReader, and XMLParser extensions.
impact:
XXE enables reading local files (e.g., /etc/passwd, wp-config.php),
SSRF to internal services, and DoS via entity expansion. PHP stream
wrappers (php://filter) allow base64-encoded file exfiltration.

title: LDAP Injection via Unsanitized Filter
description: Detects LDAP filter construction with user-controlled input without proper escaping via ldap_escape(). Covers ldap_search, ldap_list, ldap_read, and custom filter string construction in PHP applications using Active Directory or OpenLDAP.
impact:
LDAP injection enables authentication bypass, user/group enumeration,
extraction of sensitive directory attributes, and potential privilege
escalation via group membership manipulation.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via curl/file_get_contents
description: Detects SSRF where user-controlled URLs are passed to curl_exec, file_get_contents, or Guzzle HTTP client, enabling access to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, and port scanning.
impact:
SSRF enables access to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints
(AWS/GCP/Azure), port scanning of internal networks, and credential
theft from cloud IAM roles.

title: Server-Side Template Injection via Twig/Smarty/Blade
description: Detects SSTI where user-controlled input is passed to template engines (Twig, Smarty, Blade) as template source rather than template data. Enables arbitrary code execution through template engine features.

title: HTTP Header / CRLF Injection
description: Detects CRLF injection where user-controlled values are passed to header(), setcookie(), or framework response header methods without stripping newline characters. Enables HTTP response splitting, session fixation, and XSS.
impact:
CRLF injection enables HTTP response splitting, XSS injection via
injected response body, cache poisoning, and session fixation via
injected Set-Cookie headers.

title: PHP Type Juggling in Security Comparisons
description: Detects loose comparison (== instead of ===) of user input against security-sensitive values (passwords, tokens, hashes), enabling authentication bypass through PHP's type coercion. Includes strcmp() bypass and hash comparison vulnerabilities.
impact:
Type juggling enables authentication bypass, HMAC verification bypass,
and API key comparison bypass. Magic hashes (0e...) compare as equal
to 0 with loose comparison. Array injection causes strcmp() to return
NULL which equals 0 with loose comparison.

title: MongoDB NoSQL Injection via PHP Driver
description: Detects NoSQL injection where user-controlled input is passed to MongoDB queries via the PHP MongoDB driver or legacy mongo extension, enabling query operator injection and authentication bypass.
impact:
NoSQL injection enables authentication bypass, data exfiltration,
and server-side JavaScript execution via $where operator. PHP's
array parameter handling makes operator injection straightforward.

title: Mail Header Injection via mail()/PHPMailer
description: Detects email header injection where user-controlled input is passed to mail() headers, PHPMailer, or SwiftMailer recipients without proper validation, enabling spam relay, BCC injection, and content manipulation.
impact:
Mail header injection enables spam relay (sending to arbitrary
recipients via BCC injection), phishing via spoofed From headers,
and content manipulation via injected Subject/Content-Type headers.

title: Second-Order SQL Injection via Stored Data
description: Detects second-order SQL injection where previously stored data (database records, session values, file contents) is used in SQL queries without parameterization. The initial storage may be safe but subsequent use in queries creates injection opportunities.
impact:
Second-order SQL injection is particularly dangerous because it
bypasses input validation at the storage point. The payload persists
in the database and triggers when the stored data is used in
subsequent queries, potentially across different application components.

title: SQL Injection in Embedded SQL
description: Detects dynamic SQL with string concatenation in PL/I.
impact: SQL injection in PL/I mainframe programs can compromise DB2 databases.
remediation:
Use host variables in embedded SQL:
  EXEC SQL SELECT * FROM ACCOUNTS WHERE ID = :WS_ACCT_ID;

title: Buffer Overflow in PL/I
description: Detects potential buffer overflow from unsafe string operations.
impact: Injection attacks can lead to data breach, unauthorized access, or system compromise
remediation: Use parameterized queries, input validation, and output encoding

title: Hardcoded Credentials in PL/I
description: Detects hardcoded passwords in PL/I programs.
impact: Authentication and authorization flaws can lead to unauthorized access and privilege escalation
remediation: Implement strong authentication, proper session management, and principle of least privilege

title: Weak Encryption in PL/I
description: Detects custom or weak encryption implementations.
impact: Weak cryptography can be broken, compromising data confidentiality and integrity
remediation: Use industry-standard algorithms (AES-256-GCM, SHA-256+, Argon2) and proper key management

title: Sensitive Data in PUT Statement
description: Detects output of sensitive data via PUT SKIP/DISPLAY.
impact: Exposed secrets enable unauthorized access to systems, APIs, and sensitive data
remediation: Use secret management systems, environment variables, and rotate exposed credentials immediately

title: SQL Injection via EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
description: Detects dynamic SQL execution with string concatenation in PL/SQL.
impact:
PL/SQL injection can compromise the entire Oracle database,
including DBA-privileged operations.

title: SQL Injection via DBMS_SQL
description: Detects unsafe DBMS_SQL usage with string concatenation.
impact: Injection attacks can lead to data breach, unauthorized access, or system compromise
remediation: Use parameterized queries, input validation, and output encoding

title: SQL Injection in REF CURSOR
description: Detects dynamic SQL in REF CURSOR open statements.
impact: Injection attacks can lead to data breach, unauthorized access, or system compromise
remediation: Use parameterized queries, input validation, and output encoding

title: OS Command Injection via UTL_* Packages
description: Detects OS command or file access via Oracle UTL packages.
impact: Injection attacks can lead to data breach, unauthorized access, or system compromise
remediation: Use parameterized queries, input validation, and output encoding

title: Excessive Privileges (GRANT DBA)
description: Detects granting of excessive database privileges.
impact: Authentication and authorization flaws can lead to unauthorized access and privilege escalation
remediation: Implement strong authentication, proper session management, and principle of least privilege

title: Hardcoded Database Credentials
description: Detects hardcoded credentials in PL/SQL code.
impact: Authentication and authorization flaws can lead to unauthorized access and privilege escalation
remediation: Implement strong authentication, proper session management, and principle of least privilege

title: Invoker Rights Missing
description: Detects stored procedures that run with definer rights instead of invoker rights.
impact: Authentication and authorization flaws can lead to unauthorized access and privilege escalation
remediation: Implement strong authentication, proper session management, and principle of least privilege

title: Weak Encryption Algorithm
description: Detects use of weak encryption in DBMS_CRYPTO.
impact: Weak cryptography can be broken, compromising data confidentiality and integrity
remediation: Use industry-standard algorithms (AES-256-GCM, SHA-256+, Argon2) and proper key management

title: Server-Side Request Forgery via UTL_HTTP
description: Detects HTTP requests with user-controlled URLs.
impact: Server-side request forgery enables access to internal resources and cloud metadata
remediation: Validate and allowlist URLs, block private IP ranges and cloud metadata endpoints

title: File Access via UTL_FILE
description: Detects file operations with user-controlled paths.
impact: Path traversal enables reading or writing arbitrary files on the server
remediation: Canonicalize paths and verify they remain within expected base directories

title: Sensitive Data Exposure via DBMS_OUTPUT
description: Detects output of sensitive data via DBMS_OUTPUT.
impact: Exposed secrets enable unauthorized access to systems, APIs, and sensitive data
remediation: Use secret management systems, environment variables, and rotate exposed credentials immediately

title: SQL Injection via String Formatting
description: Detects SQL query construction using Python f-strings, .format(), or % string formatting with user-controlled input.
impact:
Full SQL injection enabling data exfiltration, authentication bypass,
data manipulation, and potential remote code execution through database
features like INTO OUTFILE or xp_cmdshell.
remediation:
Use parameterized queries exclusively:

Django ORM (preferred):
  User.objects.filter(username=user_input)
  User.objects.raw("SELECT * FROM auth_user WHERE id = %s", [user_id])

Django QuerySet.extra() - avoid, use annotations instead:
  MyModel.objects.annotate(val=Value(user_input)).filter(...)
